summary: The eight bombing missions hour by hour, what starts a bombing and who is in it, the bombers' fire and what their bombs take off a province, the fire that comes back, both sides' modifiers, a carrier's aircraft and the daily repair.

addresses.name: CGroundAttackOrder::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11 of ground attack and of interdiction: the order's province is land and its controller an enemy of the unit's owner (CCountry::IsEnemy). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CStrategicBombOrder::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11 of the strategic bombing, the logistical strike, the runway and the installation strike: a land province whose controller is an enemy of the unit's owner, and a `strategic_attack` above nothing in the unit's own definition. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CNavalStrikeOrder::MayBeGiven
addresses.comment: Slot 11 of the naval strike and of the convoy raid from the air: the order's province is not land. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CPortStrikeOrder::MayBeGiven

addresses.name: CNavalStrikeOrder::IsProvinceAllowed

addresses.name: CPortStrikeOrder::IsProvinceAllowed

addresses.name: CBombLogisiticsOrder::BombsStockpile
addresses.comment: Slot 31, asked by CSubUnit::BombProvince of each of the seven goods of a province's pool: yes for 0 and 1, supplies and fuel. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CStrategicBombOrder::BombsProduction
addresses.comment: Slot 32, asked by CSubUnit::BombProvince of each of the seven goods of a province's `current_producing`: yes for 3 to 6 - crude oil, metal, energy and rare materials. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::UpdateStrike
addresses.no_signature: One argument, the order; where it arrives was not read off the bytes.
addresses.comment: **The hour of ground attack, interdiction, the naval strike and the convoy raid from the air.** Nothing with `return_to_base` set, at its base's province and unfit, in a battle or in a bombing; unfit elsewhere it is told to return and the hour runs on; no fuel, or hours of grace after a bombing (CUnit +0x9C) above nothing, and it returns; nothing with a path. With no strike province (+0x68), or one that is land and no longer an enemy's, it picks one at its base where fit (slot 39). Away from the strike it is given the way there, the light at the hour of arrival is judged against the mission's `time`, and at its own base +0x7C is set to the tick and four. **Standing in the strike province with no bombing it picks again, and returns where there is none** - so the strike province is kept from sortie to sortie. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::StartStrikeMission
addresses.comment: Slot 13 of the four strike missions: a unit with a base that is not in its base's province is told to return, then CAirOrder::UpdateStrike. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::IsStrikeActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14 of ground attack, interdiction and the naval strike: no base, done; CAirOrder::UpdateStrike; CAirOrder::IsActive. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirConvoyRaid::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14 of the convoy raid from the air: its count at +0x80 down by one; in the strike province with the count under one, ResolveConvoyRaid for the unit and the count to 12; then CAirOrder::UpdateStrike and CAirOrder::IsActive. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirConvoyRaid::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39: of the mission's provinces other than the one the unit is in, the one with the highest 1000 + 1000 x the transports of every enemy convoy passing through it. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::UpdateBombing
addresses.comment: **The hour of the strategic bombing, the logistical strike, the runway and the installation strike and the port strike.** Nothing with `return_to_base` set or in a battle; **in a bombing the strike province (+0x68) is forgotten**; unfit, in its hours of grace or past its `death_date` it is told to return and the hour runs on; no fuel and it returns; nothing with a path. With no strike it picks one at its base where fit (slot 39) and returns where there is none; standing in its strike province it returns; otherwise it is given the way there, with the same judging of the light at the hour of arrival and the same +0x7C as CAirOrder::UpdateStrike. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::StartBombingMission
addresses.comment: Slot 13 of the five bombing missions: a unit with a base that is not in its base's province is told to return, then CAirOrder::UpdateBombing. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::IsBombingActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14 of the strategic bombing, the logistical strike and the runway and installation strikes: no base, done; CAirOrder::UpdateBombing; CAirOrder::IsActive. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CPortStrikeOrder::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14 of the port strike: the others', and with no strike province the order is done unless some province of the mission passes slot 37. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 3.

addresses.name: IsNightAtTick
addresses.no_signature: Two stack arguments and a province in a register; the return is IsNight's and was not read off the bytes.
addresses.comment: Whether it is night over a province at a tick: the hour of the day and the month are made out of the tick (less the zero tick, over 24; the day of the year walked down the table of month lengths) and given to IsNight. The two frames ask it of the strike province at the hour the unit will arrive. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CGroundAttackOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39. None in the unit's hours of grace. Otherwise the province after the strike province in the mission's list (the first with no strike, the first again after the last, the strike itself where it is not listed) - unless that is the strike province and some province scored above nothing, and then the best of those. **So a list of two or more is gone round in order and the score counts for a list of one.** The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x58E837..0x58E86E for the last choice.

addresses.name: CGroundAttackOrder::ScoreProvince
addresses.no_signature: stdcall-shaped with five stack arguments (order, out, province, strike, unit); the ret was not read.
addresses.comment: -10000 for the strike province; -10,000,000 where the wings already bound for the province (air units of countries at war with its controller whose order's slot 24 says yes and whose +0x68 is it) are above nothing and with the unit's own more than 3; -20000 where the unit's country knows it at under 2; otherwise the strength of the land units there of countries at war with the owner, summed unit by unit, **the running sum divided by a hundred each time a unit is not holding ground**. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.

addresses.name: CAirInterdictionOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39. Its "best" is **the last province of the list scoring above -1000**, the test being `score > -1000 or score > best`; it answers that unless the province after the strike in the list differs from the strike and the hours of grace are above nothing, and then that next one. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x58DC70..0x58DD1F: `cmp eax, 0xFFFFFC18; jg` takes the province before the compare with the best.

addresses.name: CAirInterdictionOrder::ScoreProvince
addresses.no_signature: The province arrives in EAX; three stack arguments beside it.
addresses.comment: Ground attack's score without the count of wings, the hundredth taken where a unit has no path (CUnit +0x140 under 1). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.

addresses.name: CNavalStrikeOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39. The interdiction's "best" - the last listed province scoring above -1000 - answered only where the province after the strike in the list is the strike itself or the hours of grace are above nothing; otherwise that next one. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x592EAD..0x592F19.

addresses.name: CNavalStrikeOrder::ScoreProvince
addresses.signature: void __cdecl CNavalStrikeOrder::ScoreProvince(int* out, CMapProvince* province, CMapProvince* strike, CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment: -10000 for the strike province; -10,000,000 by the count of wings bound for it as in ground attack's; -20000 where the unit's country knows it at under 2; otherwise 1000 a ship of the fleets there of countries at war with the owner. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; `add esp, 0x10` after the call at 0x592EE1.

addresses.name: CStrategicBombOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39: over the mission's provinces that pass slot 37, the highest of `industry (province modifier 15) + current_producing of crude oil, metal, energy and rare materials`, x 1000 over the anti-aircraft level (modifier 75) where that is not nothing; the first found among equals; a province that the wings already bound for it (slot 24 and slot 22 and +0x68) and the unit's own would make more than 3 on is passed over. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x58B641..0x58B662 for the five figures.

addresses.name: CBombLogisiticsOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39: the highest of `the supplies in the province's pool + infrastructure (modifier 12)`, x 1000 over the anti-aircraft level where that is not nothing. The first province stands until a higher is found. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x58C0A3..0x58C0F5; the decompiler loses the comparison.

addresses.name: CBombRunwayOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39: the highest of `1000 x the units based in the province` (the count at +0xC of its base object, CMapProvince +0x54), over the anti-aircraft level the same way. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.

addresses.name: CBombInstallationOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39: the highest radar level (province modifier 48), over the anti-aircraft level the same way. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.

addresses.name: CPortStrikeOrder::PickProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 39: the highest of `1000 a ship of the fleets in the province + the naval base (modifier 45)` where its controller is at war with the unit's owner, and nothing otherwise. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 4.

addresses.name: CBombRunwayOrder::MayBeGivenOver
addresses.comment: Slot 10, which the base answers with slot 11: over a list of provinces it frees, yes where the unit has a strategic attack and one of them has an air base (maximum above nothing) held by an enemy. The name is ours; who calls it was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CPortStrikeOrder::MayBeGivenOver
addresses.comment: Slot 10: over a list of provinces it frees, yes where one of them has a naval base (maximum above nothing) held by an enemy. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CGroundAttackOrder::ShouldBombProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 17 of ground attack: its strike province; and any province with units in it that the unit's country knows at 2 or better, where some land unit of a country at war with it is holding ground (CUnit::IsHoldingGround). **So it bombs on the way.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.

addresses.name: CAirInterdictionOrder::ShouldBombProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 17 of interdiction: a province the unit's country knows at 2 or better that has units in it, where it is the strike province or some land unit of a country at war with it has a path (CUnit +0x140 above nothing). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.

addresses.name: JoinBombingInProvince
addresses.comment: Offers a unit to the bombing a province has (+0x2FC): nothing for a unit in its hours of grace (+0x9C) or in a bombing (+0x110), for a land unit unless the bombing is of kind 5 or a fleet unless it is of kind 6; otherwise `combat->AddUnit(unit)` (slot 18), and the bombing's kind where that took it. CCombatManager::CheckForCombat calls it for an air unit whose order's slot 17 says yes, before CCombatManager::StartBombing. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the call at 0x431340 pushes the province with the unit in EDI.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::StartBombing
addresses.signature: int __stdcall CCombatManager::StartBombing(CCombatManager* manager, CMapProvince* province, CUnit* unit) @EAX
addresses.comment: **What an air unit under a bombing order does about a province that has no bombing it could join.** Nothing for a unit in a bombing or in its hours of grace (+0x9C). **Kind 4** for a land province where the order's slot 26 says yes and the controller is an enemy of the unit's owner (CCountry::IsEnemy) - a raid on the ground itself, no unit needed. Otherwise the first unit of the province, in list order, that is an air unit at its own base (the order's slot 29, and slot 17 of the bomber's province), a fleet (slot 27) or a land unit (slot 28); that, a fleet at sea, the bomber with a wing sights (ShouldStartNavalCombat); and that passes CUnit::CanEngage with the bombing flag and DefenderAcceptsBattle - **kind 6 for a fleet, 5 otherwise**. Where the province has no bombing, CCombatManager::CreateCombat; and for a strategic bombing (0x6F9) BOMBING_THREAT_IMPACT on the owner's threat (0x4F4E80) and STRAT_BOMBING_PENALTY, dated now, on the target's country or the controller's (0x5307A0), neither read further. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: Read through: the slots that pick the target, the sighting of a fleet, and the two calls a strategic bombing adds. The 'terrain byte' of the old comment is the province's is_land, and slot 0x68 is slot 26.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::CheckForCombat
addresses.signature: char __thiscall CCombatManager::CheckForCombat(CCombatManager* this, CUnit* unit, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment: **Where every combat in the game starts.** ~34 callers, all of them 'this unit's situation changed'. For any unit JoinCombatInProvince and then CCombatManager::StartCombat; a land unit in no battle then takes the province. **And for an air unit whose order's slot 17 says yes of the province**: where the province has a bombing (+0x2FC), JoinBombingInProvince; and where the unit is then in none (+0x110), CCombatManager::StartBombing. `ret 8`, `this` in ecx. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x431328..0x431354.
addresses.revises: The bombing tail has two steps, not one: the join comes before the start.

addresses.name: CUnit::CanEngage
addresses.signature: char __stdcall CUnit::CanEngage(CUnit* this@EDI, CUnit* other@stack:4, bool bombing@stack:8, CMapProvince* province@stack:12) @AL
addresses.comment: **`this` is in EDI**, `ret 0xC`. The filter CCombatManager::StartCombat and StartBombing apply to a unit standing in the province. After a war between the owners (or an undeclared one covering the province), different units and owners and neither retreating: **for a battle that is not a bombing**, the same arm, and for two air units the orders count only at a base - where this unit is at its own base its order's slot 34 and slot 25, where the other is, **this** unit's slot 34 and the **other's** slot 25. **With the bombing flag**: of two air units, the other at its own base and this unit's order's slot 29 and slot 17 of this unit's province; a fleet or a land unit as `this` only against an air unit. Either way neither a loaded land unit going nowhere. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4, for the air arm. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: The bombing flag's arm is now stated.

addresses.name: CUnitList::AllHostileTo
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CUnitList::AllHostileTo(CUnitList* list@EAX, CUnit* unit@stack:4, bool bombing@stack:8) @AL
addresses.comment: False for an empty list or no unit; otherwise true only where **every** unit of the list passes against the candidate what CUnit::CanEngage tests, the list's unit being the asker: a war between the owners (or an undeclared war covering the province, or REB), different owners, neither retreating, neither loaded - and without the bombing flag the same arm with the air units' order tests; **with it**, where both are air units the candidate at its own base and the list unit's order's slots 29 and 17, and where the list unit is a fleet or a land unit the candidate an air unit. **So the defender of a bombing is hostile to a second bomber only where it has units and no aircraft among them.** The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: The bombing flag's arm is now stated.

addresses.name: CCombat::AddUnit
addresses.comment: Slot 18. Offers a unit to a combat that already exists and lets the combat pick the side: with `a` the attacker's IsHostileTo and `d` the defender's, the unit joins the attacker where d and not a, the defender where a and not d, and neither otherwise - the side the *other* side is hostile to. **For a bombing the defender's side refuses an air unit that is not at its own base** (CUnit_IsAtOwnBase). The same body is slot 18 in all six combat classes. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: The 'global test at 0x5CDC30' is CUnit_IsAtOwnBase, asked only of an air unit in a bombing; the 'unit's own slot 17' is its IsAir.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::CreateCombat
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCombatManager::CreateCombat(CCombatManager* manager, CMapProvince* province, int kind, CUnit* attacker, CUnit* defender)
addresses.comment: The live combat factory, `ret 0x14`, five stack arguments. A jump table at 0x431604 on `kind - 1` makes one of the six combats (1 land, 2 naval, 3 air, 4 ground bombing, 5 land bombing, 6 naval bombing); then AddCombat, slot 6 (CreateCombatants), SetProvince; for kind 4 the province's controller onto the defender's countries; the attacker and the defender onto their sides (slot 12, CUnit::AttachCombat, and for a combat that is no bombing CUnit::ShowFighting). **Then every other unit of the province is offered through CCombat::AddUnit - in a bombing a land unit only to a kind 5 and a fleet only to a kind 6** - and, where the attacker's order's slot 27 says yes and the province has an owner, a port and a naval base whose maximum is above nothing, **every fleet in the port**. A bombing goes in the province's single slot (+0x2FC), any other combat on its list (+0x2EC). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md for the dead default arm. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: The bystanders' rule for a bombing is now exact: by the bombing's kind, and the port's fleets by slot 27.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::Attack
addresses.comment: **Slot 15 of CBomberCombatant.** The leaders' hours and CCombatant::GainPractical with BOMBING_DOCTRINE_INCREASE; then per unit of the side: where its order's slot 33 says yes, CCombatant::CollectFightingLandTargets; where the side then has no target, CCombatant::CollectBombTargets; and for each of its wings CBomberCombatant::FireUnit and CSubUnit::BombProvince. **The list is made afresh for every unit.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
addresses.revises: The two helpers and the call after FireUnit are now named: the second is where a province is bombed.

addresses.name: CCombatant::CollectFightingLandTargets
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombatant::CollectFightingLandTargets(CCombatant* this, CBomberCombatant* bombers, CUnit* bomber)
addresses.comment: Makes the bombers' list of targets (+0xB0 the count, +0xB4 the 1024) out of this side's land units that are in a battle: each by a roll, `Random() % 100 <= t x 100 / 1000`, t the bomber's owner's `frontline_focus` (CTechnologyStatus +0xD0) where the unit is on the front line (CLandCombatant +0xB0) of a land battle and its `reserve_focus` (+0xD4) otherwise; one that passes has every brigade with strength left added. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.

addresses.name: CCombatant::CollectBombTargets
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombatant::CollectBombTargets(CCombatant* this, CBomberCombatant* bombers, CUnit* bomber)
addresses.comment: Makes the bombers' list out of this side's units: an air unit only under the bomber's order's slot 29 and slot 17 and only at its own base, a land unit only under slot 28, a fleet only under slot 27 or a convoy raid's order (0x592); every brigade, wing or ship with strength left, 1024 at most. **A ship, under any order but the convoy raid's, only by a roll of its own**: `Random() % 100 <= the bomber's leader's skill x 10 x (1000 + naval_air_target_chance) / 1000`, CTechnologyStatus +0xD8 - the leader read off CUnit +0x12C with no test for none, which is the empty leader. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x5609CD..0x560A35 for the roll.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::FireUnit
addresses.comment: **One bombing wing's shots for a tick.** One target drawn from the side's list for all its shots (`Random() % count`); the attack by the wing's unit's order - slot 28 the soft and hard attack split by the target's softness, slot 27 or a convoy raid's order `sea_attack`, slot 29 `hard_attack`, otherwise nothing - each with a CommandEffect; shots = attack x the wing's attack product, the fraction a chance at one more; per shot an unused draw, the avoid roll against CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF, an organisation die of 3 to 9 and a strength die of 1 to 3, **a 10% chance of ten times the strength**, a ship's two divided by its hull, and then by the target's kind the six compiled-in factors and BOMB_REGIMENT/SHIP/WING_DAMAGE_MODIFIER - a brigade's strength also x (1000 + 10 x the defender's brigades) / 1000, and a ship's two x CAG_SHIP_ATTACK_STR_BONUS and _ORG_BONUS where the wing is a carrier's and the ship's fleet is in a battle. A ship left with nothing goes on the attacker's list of ships sunk. **The target's air defence is computed and discarded** - reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
addresses.revises: The critical roll multiplies the strength die by ten; the old comment had it cut by ten. The order's slots, the regiment count and the carrier's bonus are now stated.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::BombProvince
addresses.comment: **What a wing's bombs do to the province, and the one reader of `strategic_attack`.** runs = max(strategic_attack x (1000 + CommandEffect 16) / 1000 x the wing's attack product / 1000, 1000) / 1000, whole. Each run rolls `Random() % 3 + 1` and takes that many times: off each good of the pool the order's slot 31 names, a base of (the infra building's max_level - its current level) x BOMB_STRATEGIC_RESOURCES_INFRA_FRACTION x BOMB_STRATEGIC_RESOURCES - for supplies and fuel times the pool over a week of SupplyNeed, 1.2 at most; off each good of `current_producing` slot 32 names, BOMB_STRATEGIC_PRODUCTION; off each building slot 30 names, its damage_factor x BOMB_STRATEGIC_BUILDINGS x its current share of its maximum. What is taken is tallied on the side (+0x10C4, +0x10D4, +0x10B4). Called for every wing of every bombing, so a wing with no strategic attack still makes one run. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.

addresses.name: CCombatant::GainPractical
addresses.no_signature: Three stack arguments (side, the category's name, the amount); the ret was not read.
addresses.comment: For every country of a side (+0x54): CCountry::GainTechAbility for the technology category named and the amount given. The air battle calls it with AIR_DOCTRINE_INCREASE and the bombing with BOMBING_DOCTRINE_INCREASE. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::IsOutOfStrength
addresses.no_signature: The sub unit arrives in ESI.
addresses.comment: Whether a brigade, a ship or a wing has less strength than this hour's pending damage will take: for a ship the damage whole, for a brigade or a wing a hundredth of it (slots 9 and 11 of CSubUnit). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::SetSunkBy
addresses.no_signature: The ship in ECX and the sinker in EAX.
addresses.comment: Writes a ship's `sunk_by` pair (+0x9C, +0xA0) from the id of the object in EAX, or the game's no-object pair where EAX is null. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.

addresses.name: CBombTargetCombatant_CollectBombers
addresses.no_signature: The bombers' side arrives in EAX and the target side on the stack.
addresses.comment: Makes a target side's list (+0xB0 the count, +0xB4 the 1024) of every wing of the bombers with strength left. The first thing all three target combatants' slot 15 do. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 7.

addresses.name: CUnitList_SumFriendlyAirAttack
addresses.no_signature: The list arrives in EAX; the out pointer and a country tag on the stack.
addresses.comment: The sum of `air_attack` out of the unit's own definition (CUnit +0xC8) over the units of a list whose owner is a friend of a country (CCountry::IsFriend). StaticAntiAirTerm asks it of the province's units and of the fleets in its port. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 7.

addresses.name: StaticAntiAirTerm
addresses.comment: **The province's own anti-aircraft fire, in all three bombings.** Nothing where the side has no wing to fire at. n = the province's modifier 75 x (1000 + the controller's `provincial_aa_efficiency`, CTechnologyStatus +0xA0) / 1000 x STATIC_AA_SCALE / 1000, **plus one and a half times the `air_attack` of every unit standing in the province whose owner is a friend of the controller**, and of every such fleet in its port (CUnitList_SumFriendlyAirAttack; the 1500 is the compiled-in static at 0x1A88154). Shots = n / 1000 and a chance at one more; each at a wing drawn at random, an unused draw, the avoid roll, an organisation die of 3 to 10 and a strength die of 1 to 2, a 10% chance of five times the strength. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, the listing 0x5623A1..0x56248A for the two lists, and staticconst.py for the 1500.
addresses.revises: Read end to end and no longer `likely`: the second term is named, and the dice.

addresses.name: CNavalTargetCombatant::Attack
addresses.comment: Slot 15 for ships under air attack. CBombTargetCombatant_CollectBombers; with a wing to fire at, the leaders' hours and StaticAntiAirTerm; then **each ship** fires `air_attack x its own attack product` (CSubUnit +0x50) in shots at wings drawn at random: an unused draw, the avoid roll against CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF, an organisation die of 3 to 9, a strength die of 1 to 3, a 10% chance of ten times the strength. Reads no `air_defence`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 7.
addresses.revises: The dice and the order of the draws are now stated.

addresses.name: CLandTargetCombatant::Attack
addresses.comment: Slot 15 for land units under air attack. CBombTargetCombatant_CollectBombers; with a wing to fire at, the leaders' hours and StaticAntiAirTerm; then **each unit, not each brigade**, fires the `air_attack` of its own definition (CUnit +0xC8) x CUnit +0xEC x +0xF4 - the land battle's two products, which CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers has just put back to 1000, so its plain air attack. Per shot an unused draw, the avoid roll, an organisation die of 4 to 12, a strength die of 2 to 5, a 10% chance of ten times the strength. Reads no `air_defence`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 7.
addresses.revises: The dice are now stated, and that the unit's products are the reset ones.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CBomberCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CBomberCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: Slot 19 for the bombing side, on every wing: difficulty; **the naval surprise** (attack only: against a naval target, while the combat's `day` is under AIR_COMBAT_NAV_SURPRISE_ROUNDS, where an attacker's first round rolled under AIR_COMBAT_NAV_SURPRISE_CHANCE or the side had it the round before); **the air combat** (the sum over the battles on the unit's own list of AIR_COMBAT_ON_BOMBING x attackers / defenders of its air battles so far, each strength at least 1000); supplies; experience; mission efficiency (not under a move order); radio; dissent; **stacking** over every wing of the side, a carrier's wing over water counting CAG_STACKING_PENALTY; radar from the province and its neighbours held by a friend; the weather and the night on the attack alone; the leader. No base proximity and no fighter's bonus. Its two `+0x128` reads are CUnit::owner_id and not `air_defence` (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 8.
addresses.revises: Read through; it was 'not read through'.

addresses.name: CTargetCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTargetCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: **Slot 19 for all three target combatants**, on every brigade, ship and wing of the side: difficulty; the capital ships' missing screens and the fort, on the defence alone; experience; mission efficiency; supplies; radio; dissent; stacking - 10 x the side's brigades less the country's free allowance (CTechnologyStatus +0x6C), where above nothing; the night on the attack alone; the leader. **Of all of it only a ship's attack product is read**, by CNavalTargetCombatant::Attack: a land unit fires by its unit's products, which these do not touch, and nothing reads a defence. Which half each moves is in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 8.
addresses.revises: Read through; it was 'not read through'.

addresses.name: CCarrierProtection::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14: no base, done. Average organisation as a share (CUnit slot 20) under CAG_DUTY_MINIMUM_ORG_LIMIT, OrderReturnToBase. In no battle, no bombing and with no path: away from its base's province, OrderReturnToBase; and **the order's province (+0xC) becomes its base's province**. Always still going. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 10.

addresses.name: CCarrierProtection::ShouldBombProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 17: `province == the order's province` (+0xC), which slot 14 keeps at the carrier's - so a carrier's aircraft bomb ships where their carrier is. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 10.

addresses.name: RunDailyProvincePass
addresses.comment: **The daily pass over one province.** Called once per province from a plain serial loop inside RunDailyPass at 0x682E4B, on the game thread. For a simulated province, after the climate: roads = infrastructure x (1000 + local + global infrastructure) / 1000 (province modifiers 12, 13, 14), held between 10 and 1000; rate = (100 + roads) x (1000 + the controller's `repair_rate`, CTechnologyStatus +0xC4) / 1000; **each of the seven goods of `current_producing` rises by the rate to `max_producing`, and each building whose definition says `repair` by BUILDING_REPAIR_SPEED x the rate to its maximum**, the province's modifiers made again where a whole level is gained. Then the acting-capital flag +0x2B0; suppression into +0x28 via 0x49F360; the modifier rebuild 0x49F3E0 behind a local flag; revolt_risk (+0x328) at 0x49EE0F..0x49EED6; and an out-of-supply draw when +0x20 is exactly 1. **It ends by holding the pool within bounds**: each of the seven goods of a land province's `pool` between the fixed-point zero and 99999.000. ret 4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md, section 8, for the bounds. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11.
addresses.revises: Its first block was 'infrastructure and the resource pools ... scaled by the controller's +0xDF8(+0xC4)': it is the daily recovery of production and the repair of buildings, and +0xC4 is repair_rate.

struct_fields.name: takeoff_tick_plus_four
struct_fields.comment: Written by CAirOrder::UpdateStrike and CAirOrder::UpdateBombing as the tick and four, where the unit is at its own base and has just been given the way to its strike province. Its reader was not looked for; the name says only what is written. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: buildings_destroyed
struct_fields.comment: An array by the building's place in the database: what CSubUnit::BombProvince has taken off each kind of building, in thousandths of a level. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: Read from the decompiled C: `*(side +0x10B4) + i * 4` is added to.

struct_fields.name: stockpile_destroyed
struct_fields.comment: An array by goods: what CSubUnit::BombProvince has taken out of the province's pool. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.

struct_fields.name: production_destroyed
struct_fields.comment: An array by goods: what CSubUnit::BombProvince has taken off the province's `current_producing`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.

struct_fields.name: changed
struct_fields.comment: Set where a bombing, a fallen-back defender's damage or the day's repair moved the current level, and cleared where it did not. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: Read from the decompiled C: written as `old != new` by CSubUnit::BombProvince and RunDailyProvincePass.

struct_fields.name: provincial_aa_efficiency
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name. StaticAntiAirTerm multiplies the province's anti-aircraft level by one plus the controller's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 7.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0xA0; the read is at 0x56242A.

struct_fields.name: repair_rate
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name. RunDailyProvincePass multiplies the day's recovery of production and of buildings by one plus the controller's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0xC4.

struct_fields.name: frontline_focus
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name: the chance, as a share of a hundred, that a ground attack singles out a land unit on the front line of a battle (CCombatant::CollectFightingLandTargets). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0xD0.

struct_fields.name: reserve_focus
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; the same chance for a land unit in a battle and not on its front line. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0xD4.

struct_fields.name: naval_air_target_chance
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name: one plus it scales the chance, ten in a hundred for each point of the bomber's leader's skill, that a ship goes on a bomber's list of targets (CCombatant::CollectBombTargets). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0xD8.

struct_fields.name: encryption
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name. UpdateIntelFunctor_SerialBody takes the province's controller's from the looking country's `decryption` to place its radar rings (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 7). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0x3C.

struct_fields.name: decryption
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name, set against the holder's `encryption` in the radar part of the intelligence refresh. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0x40.

struct_fields.name: listening_station
struct_fields.comment: The technology effect of that name: the flag the intelligence refresh asks before it gives a country its radar rings (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 7). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py 0x537DB0 places the effect key at +0xDC, as a byte.

struct_fields.name: strategic_attack
struct_fields.comment: The `strategic_attack` key, thousandths. **Its one reader in a bombing is CSubUnit::BombProvince** (0x15FF40), which makes its whole part the number of runs a wing bombs the province with each hour, never fewer than one. The census of 2026-10-05 found no reader because it took 0x160000-0x180000 for the combat classes, and this function sits just under it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6.
struct_fields.revises: It said 'No reader in any combat function ... Unread'.
